extracted.intended_audience: filmmakers, screenwriters, and general readers interested in the Slamdance Film Festival
extracted.subtask_description: Information about the Slamdance Film Festival, its focus, programs (including the screenplay competition, DIG, Unstoppable), and the kinds of films/projects it programs, promotes, and distributes. Useful for filmmakers/screenwriters considering submitting work or studying Slamdance's selection emphases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on emerging artists
rubrics_metrics.description: The Slamdance Film Festival is an annual film festival focused on emerging artists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The festival is the main event organized by the year‑round Slamdance organization and places emphasis on discovering and elevating new filmmaking talent (examples of notable alumni include Christopher Nolan, Rian Johnson, Ari Aster, Bong Joon Ho, Lena Dunham, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on independent films with budgets under $1 million
rubrics_metrics.description: Slamdance emphasizes independent films with budgets under $1 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization's programming and identity prioritize truly independent productions; this budget emphasis is cited as a defining curatorial criterion when selecting films and promoting independent voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screenplay competition categories and top-prize structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Slamdance Screenplay Competition awards prizes to top scripts across categories (e.g., Narrative Feature, Best Horror Screenplay, Best Short Screenplay, Best Teleplay) and awards a Grand Prize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically the competition has given cash Grand Prizes (example: $10,000 Grand Prize in 2013; 2017 winners received $2,000 for Best Horror and $8,000 for Grand Prize) and awards top three scripts in each category. The page lists many annual winners and category distinctions, indicating the competition's structure and prize tiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winners may receive production, development, or distribution opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Screenplay and film winners at Slamdance have been developed into produced films or acquired for distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Drool (winner of the screenplay competition) was developed and produced after an agreement with Upload Films and premiered at Slamdance; Jug Face (2011 Grand Prize) later premiered and was picked up by Gravitas Ventures; multiple winners have led to production representation or distribution. This implies that the competition can provide tangible development/distribution pathways, not just awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of digital, interactive, and immersive works (Slamdance DIG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Slamdance integrated digital, interactive, and immersive art into its program via DIG, showcasing cutting-edge digital storytelling and interactive projects including VR and games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DIG selects projects across interactive/VR/gaming/digital storytelling formats (examples listed include VR projects, interactive games, and digital art). The program opened at Big Pictures Los Angeles and is included in the festival lineup, indicating Slamdance accepts non-traditional film media in this track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unstoppable: disability-inclusive programming criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Unstoppable is a program dedicated to films created by filmmakers with visible and non-visible disabilities, launched to address barriers to representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Started as a shorts showcase in 2021 and expanded to include feature-length films; examples of presented films include Feeling Through (2020) and Bad Survivor (2025). This program constitutes an explicit curatorial category prioritizing disabled filmmakers and accessibility/representation considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Touring and outreach selection (Slamdance on the Road)
rubrics_metrics.description: Slamdance curates a traveling showcase ('On the Road') that brings popular Slamdance films to other cities and international venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the Road selects festival films for wider theatrical exhibition and outreach in U.S. cities and abroad (examples: New York, Los Angeles, Austin, Detroit, Canada, China, Poland, France, Chile), indicating a selection metric favoring films with audience appeal or representational value for touring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and VOD promotion (Slamdance Presents / Slamdance Studios)
rubrics_metrics.description: Slamdance operates distribution efforts (Slamdance Presents / Slamdance Studios) and has partnered with platforms and exhibitors (ArcLight, Microsoft, iTunes, Amazon, Hulu, Cinedigm/New Video) to place festival films on theatrical and VOD platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slamdance has acquired and released titles, launched a streaming program on Hulu, and placed competition films on VOD marketplaces; examples include theatrical releases and VOD successes (e.g., The Resurrection of Jake the Snake hitting #1 on iTunes). This indicates a pathway and selection emphasis for films deemed suitable for commercial exhibition/distribution.
